messages:
arjun: quick heads-up — saw sustained p99 regressions on node-gpu-5 around 11:20. root cause looks like long-seq tenants monopolizing batch credits; short-seq requests queue behind and miss the fastpath kernel.

runtime-bot: perf-alert: high p99 latency (short_requests) on shard node-gpu-5. profile: https://perf.internal/runs/38271 — top: kernel_switch_hotspots + KV_evictions

maya: can we try credit-splitting between short/long lanes? idea: reserve token_budget targets per lane so short seqs get a steady slice rather than fighting in the shared queue :thinking_face:

sophie: agree. also KV behavior is amplifying it — long sequences use big KV segments and we evict small KV objects that short requests rely on. short requests then go to cold KV path and spend extra latency.

arjun: proposal sketch:
```
batching.policy: continuous
batching.targets: {"short_lane_tokens":512, "long_lane_tokens":2048}
kernel.prefs: ["fastpath_v2", "balanced_v1"]
kernel.switch_threshold: 64  # max tokens to stay on fastpath
kv.pin_small_keys: true
```
We'll implement soft-reservations: short lane gets a persistently refilled credit pool (leaky-bucket). Long lane uses leftover tokens but cannot eclipse short pool.

liam: need to be careful with fairness vs throughput tradeoff. If we cap long too hard we'll blow up overall throughput and OOM risk with KV pinning. We should A/B at 10% traffic.

sophie: telemetry to add:
- per-tenant lane credit usage
- p50/p95/p99 latency by seq_len buckets (<=32, 33-256, 257+)
- KV hit/miss per tenant, eviction churn
- kernel switch counts and durations

maya: + add a microtrace span around kernel selection so we can see pathological back-and-forths (fastpath -> balanced -> fastpath thrash).

arjun: rollout plan: 10% canary for 24h, measure short p99, overall tok/s cost, KV hit rate, and throughput. if short p99 down and overall tok/s delta < 5% accept.

liam: experiment checklist: instrumented flags, emergency rollback route, alert if short_p99 > baseline + 10% or kv_evictions increase > 15%.

maya: I'll open an RFC and a small patch set. target to land kernel flag + credit-split logic behind runtime flag next week. @sophie can you draft the telemetry dashboard?

sophie: on it. I'll also prototype a KV warmup probe: for tenants with frequent short bursts we prefetch last-N keys into LRU top.

arjun: awesome. thanks team — label this thread "experiment: credit-split + KV-warmup" and paste links when ready :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment scheduled for 2024-07-22 02:00 UTC (flag=credit_split_experiment) — owners: @maya, @arjun
